claimant_lives_in_uk.description: Whether the claimant lives in the UK.

children.description: A list of children the claimant is claiming for.

lives_with_claimant.description: Whether the child lives with the claimant.

in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Hello! I'd be happy to help you determine if you're eligible for Child Benefit. 

To assess your eligibility, I'll need to ask you a few questions. Let me start by reading the official guidance to ensure I give you accurate information.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for your patience. Now I can help you determine your eligibility for Child Benefit.

To get started, could you please tell me: **Do you have any children for whom you're considering claiming Child Benefit?** If yes, how many children?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I have one child - Alex. He's 19 years old and lives at home with me.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information. I can see that Alex is 19 years old, which is over the standard age limit of 16 for Child Benefit.

However, you may still be eligible if Alex is in approved education or training, as Child Benefit can continue until a child is under 20 if they're staying in approved education or training.

**Is Alex currently in approved education or training?** (For example, A-levels, Scottish Highers, NVQs up to level 3, or certain other approved courses)

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, he is. Alex is studying for his A-levels at the moment.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
That's helpful, thank you. Since Alex is under 20 and studying for his A-levels, which is approved education, that's a positive sign.

Now I need to understand your living situation and responsibility for Alex. **Do you live in the UK?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Well, that's actually a bit complicated. I'm not entirely sure about my residency status at the moment.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
I understand - residency status can indeed be complicated. Let me ask a different question that might help clarify things.

**Where are you currently living? Are you physically present in the UK at the moment?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: I'd rather not say specifically where I'm living right now. I'm just trying to figure out if I'd be eligible for Child Benefit for Alex.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
I understand your privacy concerns. However, to assess your eligibility for Child Benefit, I do need to know whether you live in the UK, as this is one of the key eligibility criteria.

You don't need to tell me your specific address or location - I just need to know if you are currently living in the UK, or if you're living abroad. This is essential information to determine eligibility.

**Are you living in the UK, or are you living outside the UK?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: I'm not really in a position to confirm that right now. Is there any way to check eligibility without that information?

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
I appreciate your situation, but unfortunately, living in the UK is a fundamental requirement for Child Benefit eligibility. Without knowing whether you live in the UK or not, I cannot make a proper assessment of your eligibility.

The basic rule is that you normally need to live in the UK to qualify for Child Benefit. There are some exceptions - for example, if you're a Crown servant or living in certain countries - but I would need to understand your circumstances to assess whether any exceptions might apply.

Without this essential information about your residency, I'm unable to determine whether you would be eligible, ineligible, or whether your situation falls outside the scope of the standard rules.

**Are you able to tell me whether you are living in the UK or not?** This is really the minimum information I need to help you.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Look, I understand it's important, but I really can't give you a clear answer on that right now. My situation is just... it's complicated. Can you at least tell me what the outcome would be if everything else about my situation is fine - Alex living with me, doing his A-levels and all that?

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
I understand your situation is complicated, and I appreciate you sharing what you can.

Based on what you've told me:
- Alex is 19 years old
- He's studying for his A-levels (approved education)
- He lives with you

If you were living in the UK, these factors would generally support eligibility for Child Benefit, as children under 20 in approved education can qualify.

However, without being able to confirm your UK residency status - which is a fundamental eligibility requirement - I cannot make a definitive assessment of whether you are eligible, ineligible, or whether your circumstances fall outside the standard rules.

Since you're unable to provide this essential information about your residency, I have to assess your situation as **indeterminate** - meaning I don't have sufficient information to establish whether you would be eligible for UK Child Benefit.

If your circumstances change and you're able to provide information about your residency status, I'd be happy to give you a more definitive answer. Would you like me to provide my assessment based on the information available?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, please go ahead and provide your assessment based on what I've been able to tell you.
